evidence.description: At 0x127d: mov rax, QWORD PTR [rax+0x18] loads message pointer from user struct. At 0x1281: mov rdi, rax sets it as argument. At 0x1284: call 10f0 (puts@plt) outputs the string - puts reads until null terminator with no length bound.

At 0x14e9: movzx eax, BYTE PTR [rbp-0x19] loads size. At 0x14f9: call 12ae (read_input) with rdi=message_buffer, esi=size. read_input calls read(0, buffer, size) which fills exactly 'size' bytes - no null byte is appended after the read.

gdb breakpoint at 0x1284 (puts call in view_message) with size=24 allocation: rdi=0x5555555592d0 (message buffer). Heap dump shows buffer at 0x5555555592d0-0x5555555592e7 (24 bytes of 'A'), adjacent top chunk header at 0x5555555592e8 = 0x0000000000020d21. puts reads 24 'A' bytes + 3 bytes (0x21, 0x0d, 0x02) before hitting null at offset 3 of the top chunk header.

PoC execution: add(size=24, 'A'*24), view(0). puts output = b'AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA\x21\x0d\x02' (27 bytes). Leaked 3 bytes beyond 24-byte buffer: hex=210d02, value=0x20d21 (top chunk size). Confirms puts reads beyond allocated buffer into adjacent heap memory.

Leaked bytes hex=210d02, value=0x20d21 = top chunk size. gdb confirms top chunk header at buffer+24 = 0x0000000000020d21. The 3 non-null low bytes are leaked before the null byte at offset 3 stops puts.

primitives.notes: INFO_LEAK is VERIFIED with dynamic evidence. puts() reads 3 bytes beyond the 24-byte allocated buffer, leaking the top chunk size (0x20d21). The leak is limited to heap chunk metadata (sizes), not heap/libc pointers, because chunk headers contain null bytes that stop puts before reaching fd/bk pointers. The allocation size must exactly fill the chunk's user data region (e.g., 24 for chunk 0x20) to avoid calloc zero-padding acting as a null terminator.

source.root_cause: Same as PRIM-001: puts(user->message) reads beyond buffer boundary. In this variant, the adjacent memory is a freed chunk's header rather than the top chunk.
source.description: When user 0's message buffer (size=24) is adjacent to user 1's user struct (freed via remove), puts reads 1 byte beyond the buffer: the chunk size byte (0x31) of the freed user_struct_1 chunk. The chunk header 0x0000000000000031 has a null byte at offset 1, which stops puts before it can reach the fd pointer in the freed chunk.

controlled_element.what: Message buffer content and allocation size (same as PRIM-001). Additionally, the heap layout is partially controlled via add/remove sequence to place a freed chunk adjacent to the message buffer.
controlled_element.how: Attacker adds user 0 (size=24), adds user 1 (size=24), removes user 1. This frees user_struct_1 and msg_1, placing them in tcache. user_struct_1's chunk header is adjacent to msg_0's buffer.

preconditions.description: Same as PRIM-001 PC-01: message buffer must be completely filled with non-null bytes (size=24 for chunk 0x20).
preconditions.necessity: Required for puts to read beyond the buffer boundary.

preconditions.description: A freed chunk must be adjacent to the message buffer. This is achieved by adding user 0 and user 1 (creating adjacent allocations), then removing user 1 (freeing user_struct_1 which is adjacent to msg_0).
preconditions.necessity: The freed chunk's header provides the leaked byte. Without a freed adjacent chunk, the top chunk header is leaked instead (PRIM-001).

preconditions.description: The freed chunk's header must have a non-null first byte (chunk size low byte). For user structs (calloc(0x20,1)), chunk size is 0x31, low byte 0x31 = non-null.
preconditions.necessity: If the first byte of the adjacent chunk header were null, puts would stop immediately at the buffer boundary with no leak.

alias_key_findings.alias: Chunk size 0x31 has non-null byte at offset 0, null at offset 1
alias_key_findings.implication: puts leaks only 1 byte (0x31) from the freed chunk header. The null at offset 1 prevents reaching the fd pointer at offset 8 (user data start of freed chunk). Heap pointers are NOT leakable via puts OOB read alone.

alias_key_findings.expression: fd pointer at freed_chunk+8 = 0x0000000555555559 (tcache safe-linked pointer)
alias_key_findings.alias: fd pointer is 8 bytes after the chunk header, but chunk header null at offset 1 blocks puts from reaching it
alias_key_findings.implication: The tcache fd pointer (which contains a heap address XOR'd with a random value) is NOT reachable via puts OOB read. This is a structural limitation of the puts-based leak: glibc chunk headers always contain null bytes in their upper bytes for small chunks (size < 0x100).

primitives.notes: RELATIVE_READ is VERIFIED: 1 byte of adjacent freed chunk metadata (chunk size 0x31) is leaked. The fd pointer (containing a heap address) is NOT reachable because the chunk header 0x0000000000000031 has a null byte at offset 1, which stops puts before it can reach the fd pointer at offset 8. This is a structural limitation: for any chunk size < 0x100 (which covers all user structs at 0x20 bytes and all message buffers up to 127 bytes), the chunk header's second byte is always 0x00, blocking puts from reading more than 1 byte of the header. This means BUG-002 alone cannot leak heap or libc pointers - it can only leak chunk size metadata.

primitives.notes: Confirms INFO_LEAK works across allocation sizes. The key requirement is that the allocation size exactly fills the chunk's user data region (no zero-padding from calloc). For glibc 2.39, valid sizes that achieve this: 24 (chunk 0x20), 40 (chunk 0x30), 56 (chunk 0x40), 72 (chunk 0x50), 88 (chunk 0x60), 104 (chunk 0x70), 120 (chunk 0x80). All leak 1-3 bytes of adjacent heap metadata.

non_primitives.reason: ARB_READ (arbitrary address read) is NOT achievable via BUG-002 alone. The puts-based OOB read is limited to reading adjacent heap memory until a null byte is encountered. The read address is NOT attacker-controlled - it is determined by the heap layout (adjacent chunk headers). Chunk headers always contain null bytes (for chunks < 0x100, the second byte is always 0x00), which limits the read to 1-3 bytes of chunk metadata. The fd/bk pointers in freed chunks (which contain heap addresses) are NOT reachable because the chunk header null bytes block puts before it reaches the user data region of the freed chunk. Therefore, this primitive is classified as INFO_LEAK / RELATIVE_READ, not ARB_READ.
